newsitem.title: USA: US must boost ag trade chances--USTR's Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: US must boost ag trade chances--USTR's Barshefsky.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Monday the United States "must simply enhance" the opportunity for larger U.S. agricultural exports through removal of unfair trade barriers.

Barshefsky, who is awaiting a Senate vote on her nomination to be the chief U.S. trade negotiator, said she would "elevate" the position of the ag trade office in her agency. "I am quite personally committed to agriculture," she said.

Some farm-state leaders have complained that agriculture, one of the few consistent surplus generators in U.S. trade, was overshadowed in the Clinton administration by high-tech products and intellectual property rights pacts.

As if to disprove the argument, Bashefsky used a speech at the Agriculture Department's annual Outlook Forum to list agricultural trade agreements and trade cases won under President Clinton. She also listed cases where the United States was forcefully seeking access to foreign markets.
"We must simply enhance market access opportunities for American agriculture," she said.

Barshefsky announced the United States would file a trade complaint Tuesday at the World Trade Organization against the Philippines for failing to open its ports to U.S. pork and ask WTO consultations over EU failure to modify import rules on U.S. rice and barley. A WTO complaint will be considered if negotiations later this week fail to make progress in opening the Japanese market to three additional varieties of U.S. apples.

During an impromptu news conference, she said the administration was "in a consultative stage" on potential legislation that would authorize "fast-track" authority for trade negotiations. She declined to discuss when Chile might join the North American Free Trade Agreement.
"I can't tell you that right now," she said in response to a question when a fast-track bill would be sent to Congress.

It is unusual for high-level nominees like Barshefsky to speak in public during the confirmation process. However, Barshefsky has been acting U.S. trade representative for several months and has remained active in trade matters.
